question: When was the fundamental duties involved in the constitution of India? (RPF Constable 2018 (17/02/2019))
options: 1947
1991
1976
2000
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 1976

Explanation:
The Fundamental Duties were added to the Indian Constitution in 1976 through the 42nd Amendment. This amendment inserted Article 51-A under Part IV-A of the Constitution, listing 11 fundamental duties of citizens. These duties were based on the recommendations of the Swaran Singh Committee. The original Constitution did not include fundamental duties; they were added later to instill a sense of responsibility among citizens towards the nation.

☛ Fundamental Duties are in which Part of the Constitution? → Part IV-A
☛ Which Article deals with Fundamental Duties? → Article 51-A
☛ How many Fundamental Duties are there currently? → 11
☛ Which committee recommended Fundamental Duties? → Swaran Singh Committee
question_hi: भारत के संविधान में मौलिक कर्तव्यों को कब शामिल किया गया था? (RPF Constable 2018 (17/02/2019))
options_hi: 1947

1976

Explanation:
भारत के संविधान में मौलिक कर्तव्यों को 1976 में 42वें संशोधन द्वारा शामिल किया गया। इस संशोधन के तहत संविधान के भाग IV-A में अनुच्छेद 51-A जोड़ा गया, जिसमें नागरिकों के 11 मौलिक कर्तव्यों का उल्लेख है। ये कर्तव्य स्वर्ण सिंह समिति की सिफारिशों पर आधारित थे। मूल संविधान में मौलिक कर्तव्य नहीं थे; इन्हें बाद में जोड़ा गया ताकि नागरिकों में राष्ट्र के प्रति जिम्मेदारी की भावना विकसित हो सके।

question: Who was the first Vice-President of independent India- (RPF Constable 2018 (17/02/2019))
options: R. Venkatraman
Dr. Rajendra Prasad
Dr. Zakir Hussain
Dr. Sarvapalli Radhakrishnan
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Dr. Sarvapalli Radhakrishnan

Explanation:
The first Vice-President of independent India was Dr. Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan, who served from 1952 to 1962. He was a renowned philosopher, scholar, and statesman who later became the second President of India. The Vice-President is elected indirectly by members of Parliament and serves as the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha. Article 63 of the Indian Constitution provides for the office of Vice-President. Dr. Radhakrishnan was born on September 5, 1888, and his birthday is celebrated as Teacher's Day in India. The Vice-President's term is 5 years, and the impeachment process requires a resolution passed by the Rajya Sabha.

question: In the Indian Constitution, the provision for suspending the fundamental rights during the Emergency has been taken from _____. (RPF Constable 2018 (17/02/2019))
options: American Constitution
Italian Constitution
Constitution of Germany
Constitution of the Soviet Socialist Republic (USSR) Association
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Constitution of Germany

Explanation:
The provision in the Indian Constitution for suspending fundamental rights during an Emergency is borrowed from the Weimar Constitution of Germany. This provision is covered under Article 359, which empowers the President to suspend the enforcement of fundamental rights during an Emergency. However, Articles 20 and 21 (right to life and personal liberty) cannot be suspended. This provision is a crucial part of India's Emergency powers, outlined in Part XVIII of the Constitution. India adapted this concept from Germany's Weimar Constitution to suit its own needs, ensuring a balance between national security and individual rights.

☛ Which fundamental rights cannot be suspended during an Emergency? → Articles 20 and 21
☛ Which Part of the Indian Constitution deals with Emergency provisions? → Part XVIII
☛ From which country did India borrow the idea of suspending fundamental rights during an Emergency? → Germany (Weimar Constitution)
☛ Under which Article is a National Emergency proclaimed? → Article 352
question_hi: भारतीय संविधान में आपातकाल के दौरान मौलिक अधिकारों को निलंबित करने का प्रावधान ______ से लिया गया है। (RPF Constable 2018 (17/02/2019))

इतालवी संविधान
जर्मनी का संविधान
सोवियत समाजवादी गणराज्य (USSR) एसोसिएशन का संविधान
solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है जर्मनी का संविधान

Explanation:
भारतीय संविधान में आपातकाल के दौरान मौलिक अधिकारों को निलंबित करने का प्रावधान जर्मनी के वाइमर संविधान से लिया गया है। यह प्रावधान अनुच्छेद 359 के अंतर्गत आता है, जो राष्ट्रपति को यह अधिकार देता है कि वह आपातकाल के दौरान मौलिक अधिकारों के प्रवर्तन को स्थगित कर सके। हालांकि, अनुच्छेद 20 और 21 (जीवन और व्यक्तिगत स्वतंत्रता का अधिकार) को निलंबित नहीं किया जा सकता। यह प्रावधान भारतीय संविधान की आपातकालीन शक्तियों का एक महत्वपूर्ण हिस्सा है, जो संविधान के भाग XVIII में वर्णित हैं। जर्मनी के वाइमर संविधान से यह विचार लेते हुए भारत ने इसे अपनी आवश्यकताओं के अनुरूप ढाला।

question: Who called the Preamble 'the identity card' of Indian Constitution? (RPF Constable 2018 (17/02/2019) Shift 2)
options: Chandrachud
Jawaharlal Nehru
Mahatma Gandhi
N. A. Palkhivala
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is N. A. Palkhivala

Explanation:
N. A. Palkhivala (1910-1994) was a renowned Indian jurist and economist. He called the Preamble of the Indian Constitution 'the identity card' because it reflects the soul and core principles of the Constitution. The Preamble declares India as a sovereign, socialist, secular, democratic republic and outlines the objectives of justice, liberty, equality, and fraternity. Palkhivala considered the Preamble as the key document of the Constitution, summarizing the guiding principles of governance. He compared it to an identity card that defines the nation's identity and aspirations. Palkhivala also argued in favor of the basic structure doctrine in the landmark Keshavananda Bharati case (1974). The Preamble holds a central place in constitutional interpretation and is often referred to as the soul of the Constitution. It encapsulates the philosophy and vision of the framers, serving as a beacon for the nation's journey.

☛ Which three words were added to the Preamble by the 42nd Amendment (1976)? → Socialist, Secular, Integrity
☛ How many objectives are mentioned in the Preamble? → Four: Justice, Liberty, Equality, Fraternity

question_hi: किसने प्रस्तावना को भारतीय संविधान का 'पहचान पत्र' कहा? (RPF Constable 2018 (17/02/2019) Shift 2)

solution_hi:

Explanation:
एन.ए.पालखीवाला (1910-1994) एक प्रसिद्ध भारतीय न्यायविद् और अर्थशास्त्री थे। उन्होंने भारतीय संविधान की प्रस्तावना को 'पहचान पत्र' कहा क्योंकि यह संविधान की आत्मा और मूल सिद्धांतों को दर्शाती है। प्रस्तावना में भारत को एक संप्रभु, समाजवादी, धर्मनिरपेक्ष, लोकतांत्रिक गणराज्य घोषित किया गया है तथा न्याय, स्वतंत्रता, समानता और बंधुत्व के उद्देश्यों को रेखांकित किया गया है। पालखीवाला ने प्रस्तावना को संविधान का मुख्य दस्तावेज माना, जो शासन के मार्गदर्शक सिद्धांतों को संक्षेप में प्रस्तुत करता है। उन्होंने इसकी तुलना एक पहचान पत्र से की, जो राष्ट्र की पहचान और आकांक्षाओं को परिभाषित करता है। पालखीवाला ने 1974 के केशवानंद भारती मामले में बुनियादी ढांचा सिद्धांत के पक्ष में भी तर्क दिया था। प्रस्तावना को संवैधानिक व्याख्या में केंद्रीय स्थान प्राप्त है।

question: The first Municipal Corporation in India was established in _______. (RPF Constable 2018 (17/02/2019) Shift 2)
options: Madras
Delhi
Mumbai
Allahabad
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Madras

Explanation:
The first Municipal Corporation in India was established in Madras (Chennai). It was founded in 1687 by the East India Company. The Madras Municipal Corporation is regarded as the oldest municipal corporation in India. It marked the beginning of local self-government in the country. Later, in 1726, municipal corporations were established in Calcutta and Bombay. The Madras corporation was initially set up by a charter, providing for a mayor and council for city administration. It laid the foundation for urban governance in India.

question_hi: भारत में पहला नगर निगम _______ में स्थापित किया गया था। (RPF Constable 2018 (17/02/2019) Shift 2)

दिल्ली
मुंबई

Explanation:
भारत में पहला नगर निगम मद्रास (चेन्नई) में स्थापित किया गया था। इसकी स्थापना 1687 में ईस्ट इंडिया कंपनी द्वारा की गई थी। मद्रास नगर निगम को भारत का सबसे पुराना नगर निगम माना जाता है। यह स्थानीय स्वशासन की शुरुआत का प्रतीक है। बाद में 1726 में कलकत्ता और बॉम्बे में भी नगर निगम स्थापित किए गए। मद्रास नगर निगम को प्रारंभ में एक चार्टर द्वारा स्थापित किया गया था, जिसमें शहर के प्रशासन के लिए एक मेयर और काउंसिल का प्रावधान था। यह भारत में शहरी प्रशासन की नींव थी।

question: "If the court will find that a person has held a public position that he is not an officer, then he can officially stop him from holding office or office." In what legal order is this written? (RPF Constable 2018 (17/02/2019) Shift 2)
options: Permission
Trademark Articles
Quo warranto
Prohibition
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Quo Warranto

Explanation:
This question relates to the writ of Quo Warranto, which is issued by the High Court when a person holds a public office illegally. The court asks 'by what authority' the person occupies the office. If the person fails to prove their right, they are removed from the office. This writ ensures that no unqualified person holds a public position. Other options like 'Permission', 'Trademark Articles', and 'Prohibition' are different legal writs used for various purposes. Quo Warranto is a powerful tool to prevent usurpation of public office.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ What does Quo Warranto mean? → It means 'by what authority' and is used to challenge illegal occupancy of a public office.
☛ Under which article is this writ issued? → Article 226 (High Court) and Article 32 (Supreme Court).
☛ What is the purpose of Quo Warranto? → To prevent an unqualified person from holding a public office.
☛ Against whom is this writ issued? → Only against claimants of public offices.
☛ What are the other writs? → Habeas Corpus, Mandamus, Prohibition, Certiorari, and Quo Warranto.
question_hi: "यदि न्यायालय को यह पता चले कि किसी व्यक्ति ने ऐसा सार्वजनिक पद धारण किया है कि वह अधिकारी नहीं है, तो वह उसे आधिकारिक रूप से पद या पद धारण करने से रोक सकता है।" यह किस कानूनी क्रम में लिखा गया है? (RPF Constable 2018 (17/02/2019) Shift 2)
options_hi: अनुमति
व्यापार-चिह्न लेख
अधिकार पृच्छा
निषेध
solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है अधिकार पृच्छा

Explanation:
यह प्रश्न भारतीय संविधान के अधिकार पृच्छा (Quo Warranto) रिट से संबंधित है। यह रिट उच्च न्यायालय द्वारा जारी की जाती है जब कोई व्यक्ति किसी सार्वजनिक पद पर अवैध रूप से काबिज हो। न्यायालय उससे पूछता है कि वह किस अधिकार से उस पद पर है। यदि व्यक्ति अपने अधिकार को साबित नहीं कर पाता, तो उसे पद से हटा दिया जाता है। यह रिट सार्वजनिक पदों की सुरक्षा और अयोग्य व्यक्तियों को पद धारण करने से रोकने के लिए महत्वपूर्ण है। अन्य विकल्पों में 'अनुमति', 'व्यापार-चिह्न लेख' और 'निषेध' रिट अलग-अलग मामलों में प्रयोग होते हैं।

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ अधिकार पृच्छा का अर्थ क्या है? → किसी सार्वजनिक पद पर अवैध रूप से बैठे व्यक्ति से पूछना कि वह किस अधिकार से वहां है।

question: What is the right to equality in the fundamental rights? (RPF Constable 2018 (17/01/2019) Shift 1)
options: Gender Equality
All people are equal before the law
People in the same community are the same
Similarity Depending on Social Quality
solution:

Explanation:
The Right to Equality is enshrined in Articles 14 to 18 of the Indian Constitution. Article 14 states that the State shall not deny to any person equality before the law and equal protection of the laws within the territory of India. This means that all citizens, irrespective of their gender, caste, religion, or social status, are equal in the eyes of the law. The right to equality is a fundamental right that prohibits discrimination and ensures that no person is granted special privileges. While other options like gender equality or social quality are related, the core principle is equality before the law for all individuals.

question: What does the secular state mean? (RPF Constable 2018 (17/01/2019) Shift 1)
options: Multilingual
Just following one religion
Beautification
Neutral in matters of religion
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Neutral in matters of religion

Explanation:
A secular state means that the state does not adopt any religion as official and remains neutral towards all religions. It grants religious freedom to citizens and does not discriminate on the basis of religion. The Indian Constitution ensures secularism through fundamental rights (Articles 25-28). It directs the state to refrain from interfering in religious matters and to provide equal protection to all religions. The goal of secularism is to promote social harmony and unity. India follows positive secularism, which respects all religions equally rather than being irreligious.

question: Who is the head of the State? (RPF Constable 2018 (17/01/2019) Shift 1)

question: If the parliament does not approve, the maximum period of ordinance is ________. (RPF Constable 2018 (17/01/2019) Shift 1)
options: 6 months
Limitless
6 months and 6 weeks
1 year
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 6 months and 6 weeks

Explanation:
According to Article 123 of the Indian Constitution, the President can promulgate ordinances when Parliament is not in session. The ordinance must be laid before both Houses of Parliament within 6 weeks of reassembly. If Parliament does not approve it, the ordinance ceases to operate at the end of 6 weeks from reassembly, but the maximum period of the ordinance from promulgation to the end of 6 weeks after reassembly is 6 months and 6 weeks. This period includes the time from issuance to the next session plus 6 weeks. If Parliament disapproves, the ordinance lapses and cannot be extended beyond 6 months and 6 weeks.

question: Under which article does the contingency funding of India come?   (RPF Constable 2018 (17/01/2019) Shift 3)
options: Article 267
Article 263
Article 280
Article 266
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Article 267

Explanation:
Article 267 of the Indian Constitution deals with the Contingency Fund of India. This fund is established to meet unforeseen expenses that cannot be authorized by Parliament in advance. The President can make advances from this fund to meet urgent needs, which are later approved by Parliament. It is separate from the Consolidated Fund of India. Article 266 covers the Consolidated Fund and the Public Account, while Article 263 deals with Inter-State Councils and Article 280 deals with the Finance Commission. The fund is crucial for managing emergencies and unplanned expenditures.

options_hi: मोहनदास करमचन्द गांधी
विट्ठलभाई पटेल
बाल गंगाधर तिलक
दादाभाई नौरोजी
solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है विट्ठलभाई पटेल

Explanation:
1925 में केन्द्रीय विधान सभा के अध्यक्ष विट्ठलभाई पटेल बने। वे भारत के पहले भारतीय अध्यक्ष थे जिन्होंने इस पद को सुशोभित किया। विट्ठलभाई पटेल सरदार वल्लभभाई पटेल के बड़े भाई थे और वे भारतीय राष्ट्रीय कांग्रेस के प्रमुख नेता थे। उन्होंने स्वराज पार्टी के सदस्य के रूप में कार्य किया और ब्रिटिश शासन के खिलाफ आवाज उठाई। इस चुनाव में उन्होंने सरकारी उम्मीदवार को हराया। केन्द्रीय विधान सभा भारत सरकार अधिनियम 1919 के तहत स्थापित हुई थी और यह ब्रिटिश भारत की निचली विधायिका थी।
